headline: Light rain tonight, then warm, dry weather through Friday before a cooler, wetter weekend.
summary: A weak system passing north brings light rain and drizzle tonight into Wednesday, mostly in the north Olympics, Cascades, and northern interior. High pressure then clears the skies and warms things up. Thursday reaches the upper 60s to mid 70s, and Friday is the warmest, driest day, with an isolated 80 possible in Cascade valleys. Patchy morning fog is possible Thursday, and gusty east winds in the Cascades could reach 20 to 30 mph. Unsettled weather returns this weekend as a trough dips south from Alaska, with a quick Saturday system bringing mostly rain. A cooler, wetter system arrives late Sunday and lasts through Tuesday, with snow levels near 5,000 feet and more mountain snow. Winds may be breezy, but forecasters rate the risk of advisory-level winds as low.
changes: Earlier discussions flagged a possible stronger, wetter system Sunday with coastal winds, but the latest one rates advisory-level winds as low risk and describes the late-Sunday system lasting through Tuesday. The rain expected tonight was described as light showers earlier and is now called light rain and drizzle.
